tier_reason: The README (default branch v2.1-agentzh) has one first-party number under table.clone: 'We observe 7% over-all speedup in the edgelang-fan compiler's compiling speed whose Lua is generated by the fanlang compiler', with no benchmark code, hardware, versions or method, so C. The comparison is the application before and after adopting the fork's table.clone API; the README never names upstream LuaJIT as the runtime of the 'before' run.

corrections.caveats: The only quantitative claim is a single anecdote (7% compile speed of the edgelang-fan compiler). It is credited to the new table.clone API, which the application had to be changed to call, not to a general speedup over upstream LuaJIT. The README does not say which runtime the 'before' run used, and gives no baseline version, workload size or machine. The other optimizations have no numbers. The CRC32 string hash applies only to Intel SSE 4.2 CPUs when built with -msse4.2, and the README presents it as hardening against hash collisions rather than as a speedup. The more aggressive JIT defaults (maxtrace=8000, maxrecord=16000, minstitch=3, maxmcode=40960) are said to 'help large OpenResty Lua applications'. Issue #224 ('luajit vs luajit2') asks how the branch differs from upstream and has no answers or numbers. The code is Lua-facing, but the fork is a drop-in LuaJIT C library that can be embedded from C++. This is a maintained branch of the already-listed LuaJIT/LuaJIT entry: GitHub does not mark it as a fork, and the README says it 'is not to be considered a fork' because it syncs with upstream regularly. The kostya/benchmarks numbers in the LuaJIT entry were measured on a binary built from this branch.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 1.4k stars, 251 forks; OpenResty's maintained LuaJIT branch, bundled with OpenResty

notes: The claim is quoted exactly from the README and the metadata checks out: MIT (COPYRIGHT file), last commit 2026-09-17 'PPC: Call libm helpers via private GOT instead of the PLT (#271)', active, not archived. The entry overlaps the listed https://github.com/luajit/luajit entry, whose kostya benchmark ran a binary built from this branch. The orchestrator may fold it as a duplicate (fork of a listed project) or keep it for its own extensions. Either way the shortcomings are: single anecdotal 7%, no methodology, and the comparison is against the application without table.clone rather than an explicit run on upstream LuaJIT.
